html:
A Chinese Buddhist monk who walked from China to India and back between 629 and 645, then spent his last years translating the texts he brought home. He lived under the early Tang dynasty.

Unhappy with the muddled Chinese versions of Buddhist scripture, he left Chang'an against an imperial ban on travel. His route ran through the oasis cities of Central Asia and over the mountains into India. There he studied for years at the great monastery of Nalanda. The story of this trip is told on the page for his journey to India.

He came home with hundreds of texts. Emperor Taizong forgave him and backed his work. With a team of helpers he translated a large share of them, and the Great Wild Goose Pagoda was built to hold them. He also wrote a record of the lands he passed through, still a key source for the history of Central Asia and India.

Centuries later his trip became the core of the novel Journey to the West.
sum: A Chinese Buddhist monk who walked from China to India and back between 629 and 645, then spent his last years translating the texts he brought home. He lived under the early Tang dynasty.
